marks.gloss_en: מסייע ליה לרבי אילעא -- the baraita's 'whoever does not say covenant and Torah... and David's kingship... has not fulfilled his obligation' is R' Il'a's dictum word for word

R' Il'a (R' Yaakov bar Acha, in the name of our master): whoever did not say covenant and Torah in the blessing of the land and the kingship of David's house in 'who builds Jerusalem' has not fulfilled his obligation
מאן דאמר צריכה מלכות קסבר דרבנן -- the one requiring kingship holds the blessing is rabbinic
ומאן דאמר אינה צריכה מלכות קסבר דאורייתא -- the one not requiring kingship holds the blessing is Torah-law
one says: 'who is good and does good' requires [mention of God's] kingship
...and that [the covenant] was given with thirteen covenants
R' Abba: one must say thanks in it at the beginning and at the end
whoever closes the blessing of the land with 'who bequeaths lands' and 'who builds Jerusalem' with 'who saves Israel' is an ignoramus
משום שנאמר ״בונה ירושלים ה׳ נדחי ישראל יכנס״ -- the building of Jerusalem is the gathering of Israel, so 'Who builds Jerusalem' closes even a blessing opened with mercy on Israel
Rav Sheshet: if he opened with 'have mercy on Your people Israel', he closes with 'Who redeems Israel'
ואמאי לא אמרת? כדרב חננאל אמר רב: לא אמר ברית ותורה ומלכות -- יצא
וזקפיה רב ששת לקועיה עלי כחויא -- Rav Sheshet stiffened his neck at me like a snake; ואמאי? דלא אמרי לא ברית ולא תורה ולא מלכות
ואת שבקת כל הני תנאי ואמוראי ועבדת כרב?! -- you left all these tannaim (the baraita, 49a.3) and amoraim (R' Il'a in R' Yaakov bar Acha's name, 49a.4) and acted as Rav?
R' Zeira to Rav Chisda: let the master come and teach
גבורתא למחתם בתרתי! והתניא רבי אומר: אין חותמין בשתים -- what prowess, to close with two! was it not taught that one does not close with two?
Rabba bar Rav Huna came to the Exilarch's house; he opened with one and closed with two
איתיביה לוי לרבי: ״על הארץ ועל המזון״! -- a closing with two
ארץ דמפקא מזון -- a land that brings forth food: one theme (= p_eretz_demafka_mazon)
״על הארץ ועל הפירות״! -- a closing with two
ארץ דמפקא פירות -- a land that brings forth fruit (= p_eretz_demafka_perot)
[the closing] 'for the land and for the food'
״מקדש ישראל והזמנים״! -- a closing with two
ישראל דקדשינהו לזמנים -- Israel, who sanctify the seasons (= p_yisrael_mekadshei_zmanim)
״מקדש ישראל וראשי חדשים״! -- a closing with two
ישראל דקדשינהו לראשי חדשים -- Israel, who sanctify the New Moons (= p_yisrael_mekadshei_rashei_chodashim)
[the closing] 'Who sanctifies Israel and the seasons'
״מקדש השבת וישראל והזמנים״! -- a closing with more than one
חוץ מזו -- except for this one (= p_chutz_mizo; the stam's ומאי שנא against it is the necessity nec_umai_shna)
[the closing] 'Who sanctifies the Shabbat and Israel and the seasons'
(the literal wording's implication, entertained and rejected) one closes the building-of-Jerusalem blessing with 'Who redeems Israel' and NOT with 'Who builds Jerusalem'
the reason one does not close with two: because one does not perform mitzvot in bundles
אי הכי ניבעי תלת -- חדא דידה, וחדא דבונה ירושלים, וחדא דברכת הארץ! ואי ברכת הארץ לא, משום דהויא ברכה הסמוכה לחברתה -- בונה ירושלים נמי לא תיבעי, דהויא ברכה הסמוכה לחברתה

הוא הדין דאפילו בונה ירושלים נמי לא בעיא; איידי דאמר מלכות בית דוד, לאו אורח ארעא דלא אמר מלכות שמים -- conceded that בונה ירושלים does not strictly need it; the kingship of Heaven is said there because the kingship of David's house is
Rav Pappa: this is what he says -- it requires two kingships besides its own
the blessing 'Who is good and does good' requires [mention of God's] kingship
one who erred and did not mention Shabbat says: Blessed... Who gave Shabbatot for rest to His people Israel in love, for a sign and a covenant; Blessed... Who sanctifies the Shabbat
one who erred and did not mention the festival says: Blessed... Who gave festivals to His people Israel for joy and remembrance; Blessed... Who sanctifies Israel and the seasons
one who erred and did not mention the New Moon says: Blessed... Who gave New Moons to His people Israel for remembrance
